auth.api_key_invalid: That API key is not valid.
auth.api_key_read_denied: This needs the web app, signed in. An API key reads everything except {exclusions}.
auth.api_key_throttled: Too many bad API keys from this address. Wait a moment and try again.
auth.api_key_write_denied: This needs the web app, signed in. An API key writes only these: {permissions}.
auth.arm_deletion_password_mismatch: That password didn't match. Deletion stays off.
auth.csrf_blocked: This request was blocked by Reaper's CSRF protection.
auth.forget_watch_password_mismatch: That password didn't match. The record was kept.
auth.forward_origin_has_path: That address must be just the site, with nothing after it.
auth.forward_origin_invalid: That address must start with http:// or https://.
auth.login_account_unreadable: Signed in to Plex, but could not read the account.
auth.login_check_failed: Could not reach Plex to check the sign-in.
auth.login_request_invalid: This sign-in is no longer valid. Please start again.
auth.login_request_timed_out: This sign-in timed out. Please start again.
auth.password_hashing_busy: The server is busy checking passwords. Please try again shortly.
auth.plex_not_owner: That Plex account does not own this server, so it cannot administer Reaper. Sign in as the server owner, or use a local account.
auth.recovery_link_invalid: That recovery link is invalid, expired, or already used.
auth.recovery_no_admin: The recovery code was valid, but this install has no admin account yet. Sign in with Plex to claim the server, or on Docker and snap run: reaper-admin create-admin --username admin
auth.sign_in_busy: The server is busy verifying sign-ins. Please try again shortly.
auth.too_many_attempts: Too many attempts. Please wait and try again.

backup.no_password_set: Set an admin password first. It's what confirms a restore.
backup.reap_in_progress: A reap is running. Let it finish or stop it, then restart Reaper.
backup.restore_not_waiting: There's no restore waiting, so nothing was stopped.
backup.upload_too_large: That file is too large to be a Reaper backup.

fairness.needs_seerr_and_tautulli: Scales needs a Seerr and a Tautulli instance: Seerr for who requested what, Tautulli for who watched it. Configure them in Settings.
fairness.person_not_found: No one by that id is in the last scan.

instance.address_empty: {service} answered, but there is nothing at this address. Check for a missing or extra path at the end of the URL.
instance.auth_refused: {service} refused the API key. Copy it again from its own settings.
instance.bad_address: That isn't an address Reaper can use. Start it with http:// or https://.
instance.bad_body: The address answered, but not with data from {service}. Check the URL.
instance.cert_rejected: The server's certificate was rejected. It may have expired, or be for a different address, or something may be sitting between Reaper and the server.
instance.cert_unknown_authority: The server's certificate is signed by an authority this machine doesn't know. Only turn off the certificate check if this is your own server on your own network: your API key travels on this connection.
instance.connect_timed_out: Couldn't open a connection to the server in time.
instance.connection_broke: The connection to the server broke before it answered.
instance.rate_limited: {service} asked Reaper to slow down. Wait a moment and test again.
instance.read_timed_out: The server didn't answer in time.
instance.redirected: The server sent Reaper somewhere else, and Reaper won't send your API key to a different address. Check the URL and anything proxying it.
instance.refused: {service} answered, but turned the request down. Check the API key first, then the URL.
instance.server_error: {service} reported a problem of its own (HTTP {status}). Check its log.
instance.unreachable: Couldn't reach the server at this address. Check the URL and port, and that the service is running.
instance.unrecognized: Couldn't connect. The full reason is in Reaper's log.

instances.required_fields: A name, a URL and an API key are all required.
instances.singleton_exists: Reaper uses one {kind}. It reads a single Plex server's watch history, and Reaper connects to one Plex. Edit the one you have, or remove it and add a different one.
instances.wrong_kind_for_root_folders: Only Sonarr and Radarr have root folders to map to a Plex library.
instances.wrong_kind_for_seerr_services: Only Seerr portals have request services to map to an instance.

integration.cross_origin_redirect_refused: The service tried to redirect somewhere else. Reaper won't send your credentials there.
integration.history_rows_unservable: {count} watch-history rows couldn't be read, so the sweep stopped.
integration.http_failure: The service answered with an error (HTTP {status}).
integration.imdb_list_truncated: That list came back too short to trust, so Reaper left the stored one in place.
integration.keep_tag_missing: The keep tag {names} doesn't exist there anymore, so anything that used to carry it is no longer protected. The keep list was left as it was, so add the tag back or take it out of your keep tags.
integration.redirect_missing_location: The download redirected without saying where to.
integration.refused_redirect: The service redirected instead of answering (HTTP {status}).
integration.tautulli_write_refused: Tautulli command {cmd} isn't on Reaper's read-only allow-list. Reaper never writes to Tautulli.
integration.timed_out: Timed out waiting for an answer.
integration.too_many_redirects: The service kept redirecting and never answered.
integration.unexpected_shape: {path} sent back something Reaper couldn't read.
integration.update_check_incomplete: GitHub's answer didn't include what Reaper needed to check for updates.
integration.write_not_declared: Blocked {method} {path}: this mutation wasn't declared to the action journal. Destructive calls must go through the action executor so that they are recorded before they are sent.
integration.write_shelf_blocked: Blocked {method} to Plex (Leaving Soon shelf). Turn deletion on, or turn on "Update while read-only" under Settings, Plex, Leaving Soon to allow this reversible shelf write while Reaper is read-only.

leaving_soon.degraded: The last scan couldn't be trusted, so the shelf wasn't updated. Run a scan that finishes cleanly first.
leaving_soon.disabled: Leaving Soon is off. Turn it on in Settings, under Plex, and Reaper will keep the shelf up to date.
leaving_soon.unlinked: Leaving Soon needs a linked Plex server. Link one in Settings first.

lists.collection_required: Say which collection in that library to read.
lists.imdb_choice_required: Pick one of the IMDb presets, or paste a list id instead.
lists.imdb_id_invalid: Paste the list's id or URL. An IMDb list id looks like ls000000000.
lists.library_required: Say which Plex library to look in.
lists.name_exists: You already have a list with that name. Pick another.
lists.name_has_comma: A list name can't have a comma in it. Reaper separates names with one.
lists.name_required: Give the list a name, so you can pick it out on the Policy screen.
lists.name_too_long: That name is too long. Keep it under 100 characters.
lists.not_found: That list no longer exists. Reload the page.
lists.registry_unreadable: One of your lists is saved in a form Reaper can't read, so it didn't check any of them. Open that list, set it up again, and save it.
lists.source_required: Pick where the list comes from.
lists.tags_required: Add at least one tag, spelled as it appears in Sonarr or Radarr.

password.too_short: Use at least {min_length, plural, one {# character} other {# characters}}.

plan.instance_orphaned: Some of these items were found by a Radarr that is no longer connected, so Reaper cannot remove them. Reconnect it, or run a new scan to drop them from the list.
plan.items_not_condemned: These items are not condemned in this snapshot, so they cannot be reaped: {keys}.
plan.items_spared: These items are spared, so they will not be reaped: {keys}. Remove the spare first if you really mean to delete them.
plan.items_unmeasured: Reaper couldn't measure the size of these items, so it won't reap them: {keys}. Check them in Sonarr or Radarr, then run a new scan.
plan.media_key_unroutable: Cannot route media_key "{media_key}" to an instance.
plan.no_canary: Reaper couldn't measure any of these items, so it has nothing safe to test the run on. The first thing a run deletes has to be something whose size it knows. Check these in Sonarr or Radarr, then run a new scan.
plan.nothing_condemned: Nothing is condemned in this snapshot; there is no plan to build.
plan.season_media_key_not_sonarr: A season media_key must be sonarr, got "{media_key}".
plan.selection_empty: No items were selected to reap.
plan.snapshot_degraded: That scan came back incomplete, so Reaper won't act on it. Fix the source and scan again. {reason}
plan.unmeasured_over_limit: This plan holds {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} Reaper couldn't measure, over your limit of {limit, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} per run. The plan is refused rather than trimmed: which of them gets deleted must not come down to the order they were listed in. Raise the limit, or reap fewer items at once.
plan.unmeasured_seasons: Reaper couldn't measure any of the seasons it would remove from {keys}, so there is nothing here it can reap. Check them in Sonarr, then run a new scan.
plan.unmeasured_sort_key: {media_key} has no measured size to order by.

plex.connection_address_invalid: The server address must be a full web address, like https://192.0.2.10:32400.
plex.connection_probe_failed: Couldn't reach a Plex server at that address, so nothing was changed. Check the address and port, and whether the certificate check should be off.
plex.connection_wrong_server: That address is a different Plex server, so nothing was changed. Reaper is linked to {expected_name}; use an address for that server, or link the other one instead.
plex.link_account_unreadable: Signed in to Plex, but could not read the account.
plex.link_ambiguous_name: This account owns more than one server named "{choice}". Pick by machine identifier instead: {ids}.
plex.link_check_failed: Could not reach Plex to check the link.
plex.link_choice_not_found: No server this account owns matches "{choice}". It owns: {names}. Start the sign-in again and pick one of those.
plex.link_not_owner: Signed in as "{username}", but that account does not own a Plex server. Reaper must be linked by the server owner: it is going to be given permission to delete media.
plex.link_request_invalid: This link request is no longer valid. Please start again.
plex.link_request_timed_out: This link request timed out. Please start again.
plex.link_timed_out: Sign-in was not completed in time. Nothing was saved.
plex.link_unreachable: Found your server ("{name}") but could not reach it on any of its {count, plural, one {# advertised address} other {# advertised addresses}}. Reaper has to talk to the server directly; check that it is running and reachable from this host.
plex.no_password_set_for_watch_reset: Set an admin password first. It's what confirms forgetting the record.
plex.not_linked: No Plex server is linked yet. Link one first.
plex.switch_owned_servers_failed: Could not ask plex.tv which servers this account owns: {error}
plex.verify_tls_no_server: No Plex server is linked yet. Link one before changing this.
plex.web_url_invalid: The Plex web address must be a full web address, like https://192.0.2.10:32400.

plexclient.paging_failed: Reaper couldn't read all of {what} from Plex.
plexclient.streams_unreadable: Could not read active sessions from Plex ({detail}). Refusing to delete: not being able to see who is watching is not the same as nobody watching.
plexclient.trash_count_failed: Couldn't count the trash in section {section}.

policy.custom_rule_floor_not_below_saturation: floor ({floor}) must be below saturate_at ({saturate_at}), or the rule is either always off or always at full pressure.
policy.custom_rule_name_collides: "{name}" is the name of a built-in signal. Give your rule a different name so the score breakdown cannot confuse the two.
policy.custom_rule_not_numeric: "{field_label}" is not a number, so it cannot be graded. Use a yes/no rule.
policy.duplicate_custom_rule_name: Two custom rules share a name; the second would silently double-count.
policy.duplicate_gate: A gate is configured twice; the second would silently win.
policy.duplicate_keep_rule_name: Two keep rules share a name; the second would silently double-count.
policy.duplicate_rating_source: The same rating source is listed twice. Set one bar per source, or the second would silently win.
policy.duplicate_signal: A signal is configured twice; the second would silently win.
policy.field_needs_list_value: "{field_label}" needs at least one value to match.
policy.field_value_has_comma: "{field_label}" can't match a value with a comma in it. Reaper separates values with one, so pick a single one.
policy.field_wrong_lane: "{field_label}" cannot be used to {use}. It only works as {allowed}.
policy.field_wrong_lane_condemn: "{field_label}" cannot be used to remove things.
policy.field_wrong_operator: "{field_label}" cannot be compared with "{op}". It works with {allowed}.
policy.gate_dormancy_floor_low: Give titles at least 5 days before removing them. To remove things faster than that, switch this protection off with its toggle rather than setting it this low.
policy.gate_popularity_floor_zero: Keeping anything watched by 0 people would protect your whole library. Set it to at least 1, or switch this protection off instead.
policy.gate_returned_floor_zero: A title that came back has to be kept for at least a day. To stop keeping them at all, switch this protection off with its toggle.
policy.keep_rule_missing_list: Say which list this keep rule is about.
policy.keep_rule_name_collides_rewatch: "{name}" is the name of the built-in rewatch keep. Give your rule a different name so the score breakdown cannot confuse the two.
policy.keep_rule_not_a_list: "{field_label}" is not a list, so it cannot be graded. Use a protection instead.
policy.keep_rule_not_numeric: "{field_label}" is not a number, so it cannot be graded. Use a protection instead.
policy.keep_rule_unexpected_list_value: "{field_label}" is a number, so this rule ramps; it does not take a list name.
policy.probe_range_invalid: That range doesn't work: the starting point has to come before the far end.
policy.probe_unprobable: Reaper can't try values against that rule.
policy.rating_vote_floor_on_percentage: {source} is a percentage with no vote count, so a vote floor on it would do nothing. Leave the votes at 0 for this source.
policy.rating_vote_floor_zero: A vote floor of 0 makes the bar on {source} meaningless: it would protect a high score drawn from a handful of votes. Use at least 1 (1000 is a sensible default).
policy.retired_gate: That protection is left over from an older version and can't be saved. Turn it off, then save.
policy.run_cap_exceeds_rolling_cap_bytes: A single run may delete more bytes than the entire 30-day budget.
policy.run_cap_exceeds_rolling_cap_items: A single run may delete {run_cap} items but the 30-day cap is {rolling_cap}. The rolling cap would be meaningless.
policy.signal_floor_not_below_saturation: floor ({floor}) must be below saturate_at ({saturate_at}), or the signal is either always off or always at full pressure.
policy.unmeasured_cap_exceeds_run_cap: A run may delete {unmeasured_cap} items with an unknown size but only {run_cap} items in total. Lower the first number, or raise the second.
policy.weights_over_100: Your rules add up to {total} points. Take {amount} away before saving. Removal points always total 100, so each one is worth the same wherever you spend it.
policy.weights_under_100: Your rules add up to {total} points. Give out the other {amount} before saving. Removal points always total 100, so each one is worth the same wherever you spend it.

poster.no_tautulli: No Tautulli configured to fetch artwork from.

reap.already_claimed: Run {run_id} was already claimed by another request. A run executes once.
reap.bytes_over_rolling_cap: This run would delete {gb} GB on top of the {past_gb} GB already deleted in the last 30 days, over the rolling cap of {cap_gb} GB. It stops rather than deleting just part. Wait for the window to pass, raise the cap, or turn limits off in Policy, under Pace and limits.
reap.bytes_over_run_cap: This plan would remove {gb} GB, over your per-run cap of {cap_gb} GB. It stops rather than deleting just part. Raise the cap or turn limits off in Policy, under Pace and limits.
reap.canary_failed: The first item, the test item ("{title}"), did not finish the way Reaper expected: {detail}. Stopping now, before anything else is touched.
reap.canceled: The run was stopped before it finished.

check.being_watched: Someone is watching it right now. Kept.
check.exclusion_confirmed: Import exclusion confirmed. It won't re-download
check.exclusion_off: Import exclusion off for this Radarr, so none was added
check.grew_since_approved: It grew since you approved it. Kept.
check.hand_reap_removed: No longer marked to reap by hand. Kept.
check.no_approved_size: No size was recorded for it at scan time. Kept.
check.no_plex_match: No Plex match, so we can't confirm it's idle. Kept.
check.not_in_confirmed_run: Not part of the run you confirmed. Kept.
check.not_played_since: Not played since you approved it
check.not_watching: Nobody was watching it right now
check.played_since_approval: It was played since you approved the plan. Kept.
check.season_changed_unmonitored: It changed while Reaper was working. The season was left unmonitored.
check.season_no_files_kept: No files left to remove. Kept.
check.season_no_files_unmonitored: No files left to remove. The season was left unmonitored.
check.season_unmonitor_confirmed: Confirmed the season is no longer monitored
check.size_unconfirmed: Couldn't confirm its current size. Kept.
check.spared_by_hand: You spared this by hand. Kept.

reap.deletion_disabled_mid_run: Deletion was turned off while this run was in progress, so the run stopped here. Anything already deleted stays deleted; nothing further was sent.
reap.item_failed_unexplained: The run stopped at "{title}". Reaper could not tell what went wrong there, so it did not touch anything after it. Anything already removed stays removed. The details are in the run's own list and in the log.
reap.items_over_rolling_cap: This run would delete {items, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} on top of the {past_items, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} already deleted in the last 30 days, over the rolling cap of {cap, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}. It stops rather than deleting just part. Wait for the window to pass, raise the cap, or turn limits off in Policy, under Pace and limits.
reap.items_over_run_cap: This plan would remove {items, plural, one {# title} other {# titles}}, over your per-run cap of {cap, plural, one {# title} other {# titles}}. It stops rather than deleting just part, because which titles go must never come down to sort order. Raise the cap or turn limits off in Policy, under Pace and limits.
reap.journal_halt: Reaper could not save its record of what it just did, so it stopped before touching anything else. Anything already removed stays removed. Check the free space and permissions on Reaper's data folder.
reap.lists_changed: Your protection lists changed after this plan was approved, so the plan is out of date and nothing was deleted. Run a new scan, then review and plan again.
reap.manifest_changed: The condemned set changed since this plan was approved: an item was added, removed, or resized. The approval was for a different plan and is void. Re-scan, re-review, and approve the new plan.
reap.no_arm_check: Refusing a real run without a live arm check: turning deletion off could not stop a run already in progress.
reap.no_clients_configured: Refusing a real run with no clients configured: there is nothing to issue the delete through, and no way to check who is watching.
reap.not_runnable: Run {run_id} is {state}, not runnable. A run executes once.
reap.overrides_unreadable: Reaper could not re-check your keep and remove decisions, so the run stopped here rather than risk deleting something you just kept. Anything already deleted stays deleted; nothing further was sent.
reap.policy_changed: Your policy changed after this plan was approved, so the plan is out of date and nothing was deleted. Run a new scan, then review and plan again.
reap.radarr_instance_missing: No Radarr instance {instance_id} is configured, but the plan targets it. Refusing to guess which server to delete from.
reap.sonarr_instance_missing: No Sonarr instance {instance_id} is configured, but the plan targets it. Refusing to guess which server to delete from.

step.being_watched: Someone is watching it right now.
step.exclusion_unconfirmed: The file was removed, but Reaper could not confirm the import exclusion, so a re-request could download it again.
step.grew_since_approved_movie: The file is bigger now ({live_gb} GB) than when it was approved ({approved_gb} GB), so it was likely upgraded since the scan. Kept. Run a new scan to review it at its current size.
step.grew_since_approved_season: This season is bigger now ({live_gb} GB) than when it was approved ({approved_gb} GB), so its files likely changed since the scan. Kept. Run a new scan to review it at its current size.
step.hand_reap_removed: The hand reap on this was removed, so it is kept.
step.item_unexpected: An unexpected error stopped this item: {error}
step.movie_deleted_no_exclusion: Deleted. Import exclusion off for this Radarr.
step.movie_not_removed: Radarr accepted the delete but the movie is still there. Nothing was removed.
step.movie_removal_unconfirmed: Radarr accepted the delete, but Reaper could not reach it again to confirm the file is gone. It is counted against your limits as removed.
step.no_approved_size: Reaper never got a size for this when it was scanned, so it cannot confirm this is what you approved. Kept.
step.no_plex_match: Plex has no rating key for this item, so Reaper cannot confirm nobody is watching it. Spared.
step.no_tmdb_id: Radarr lists no TMDB id for this movie, so the import exclusion could never be verified after deleting. The file was kept. Fix the movie's identification in Radarr, then plan again.
step.not_in_confirmed_run: This was not part of the run you confirmed, so it is kept.
step.played_since_approval: Played since the plan was approved.
step.season_files_arrived: {count} more file(s) landed in season {season} while Reaper was working, so it is no longer what was approved. Nothing was deleted, and the season was left unmonitored. Run a new scan to review it as it is now.
step.season_files_remain: {count} episode file(s) for season {season} remain after the delete. Not confirmed.
step.season_files_vanished: Sonarr no longer lists any file for season {season}, so nothing was deleted. The season was left unmonitored.
step.season_no_files: Sonarr lists no files for season {season}, so there is nothing to delete. Kept.
step.season_pruned: Season {season} pruned: {count} file(s) deleted, unmonitor verified.
step.season_removal_unconfirmed: Sonarr accepted the delete for season {season}, but Reaper could not reach it again to confirm the files are gone. They are counted against your limits as removed.
step.size_unconfirmed_movie: Radarr did not report this movie's current size, so Reaper cannot confirm it is still the file that was approved. Kept.
step.size_unconfirmed_season: Sonarr did not report a size for every file in this season, so Reaper cannot confirm it is still what was approved. Kept.
step.spared_by_hand: You spared this by hand, so it is kept even though it was in the plan.
step.transport_guard_blocked: The transport guard blocked the delete: {error}
step.unmonitor_not_verified: Unmonitor did not take. Refused to delete files while still monitored.
step.unmonitor_verify_failed: The season is still monitored after the unmonitor. Not deleting files.

reap.stopped_by_operator: You stopped this run, so it halted here. Anything already removed stays removed; nothing further was sent.
reap.unexpected: The reap hit a problem it didn't expect: {error}
reap.unmeasured_for_caps: Reaper couldn't measure the size of these items, so it can't check the run against your limits: {keys}. The run is aborted.
reap.unmeasured_over_limit: This run would delete {unmeasured, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} Reaper couldn't measure, over your limit of {limit, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} per run. It stops rather than deleting just part. Raise the unknown-size allowance in Policy, under Pace and limits.

restore.archive_too_large: This backup is larger than Reaper can restore.
restore.database_unreadable: The database inside this backup isn't readable.
restore.database_unverifiable: The database in this backup couldn't be verified. It may be damaged, or not a Reaper backup.

restore.missing_contents: This isn't a Reaper backup: some of its contents are missing.
restore.missing_key: This backup is missing its encryption key and can't be restored.

restore.not_a_backup: This isn't a Reaper backup file.
restore.nothing_staged: There's no backup ready to restore. Choose a file first.
restore.prepare_failed: Reaper couldn't prepare this backup. Nothing was restored.
restore.schema_unverifiable: Reaper couldn't check this backup against its own version. Try again, or update Reaper.
restore.staged_changed: The staged backup changed since you reviewed it. Check it again before restoring.
restore.unreadable_archive: This isn't a readable Reaper backup file.

review.show_not_in_scan: That show is not in the latest scan.

runs.already_running: A reap is already running. Wait for it to finish, or stop it, first.
runs.confirmation_mismatch: That confirmation does not match this plan. Expected: {expected}. The plan may have changed since the page loaded. Reload, review, and confirm again.
runs.limits_unreadable: Reaper couldn't read the limits you saved, so it won't reap. Open Policy, go to Pace and limits, and save your limits again.

runs.not_running: That run is not currently running.

safety.deletion_off: Deletion is turned off, so Reaper can look but can't remove anything. Turn it on in Policy → Deletion when you're ready.
safety.recovery_mode_active: Recovery mode is on, so Reaper can look but can't remove anything. Turn it off and restart.

scan.already_running: A scan is already running. Wait for it to finish, then start another.
scan.gate_unimplemented: Policy enables the "{gate}" protection, but Reaper has no implementation for it. Refusing to scan rather than silently skipping a protection you asked for.
scan.list_gate_missing_list: A protection you set up is pointing at a list that is no longer there, so the scan stopped instead of leaving titles unprotected. Add the list back on Settings, Lists, then open Policy and save. Turning that protection off instead drops it for good.
scan.missing_sources: A scan needs a Tautulli instance plus at least one Radarr or Sonarr. Add them in Settings first.
scan.source_unreachable: Reaper couldn't reach one of your sources: {error}
scan.unexpected: The scan hit a problem it didn't expect: {error}

settings.bad_cron: That is not a valid schedule: {reason}. Use cron form, e.g. '30 4 * * *'.
settings.desktop_only: These settings exist only on the Windows and macOS apps.

settings.dock_icon_macos_only: The Dock icon setting exists only on the macOS app.
settings.external_url_invalid: The external URL must be a full web address, like https://192.0.2.10:8989.
settings.folder_list_unreachable: Could not read the folder list: {error}

fieldHelp.days_unwatched: Counted from the last play. If it has never been played, it is counted from whichever is later: when it was added, or the start of your watch history. Never from 1970.
fieldHelp.genre: The genres recorded for this title. Use "contains" to match one genre within a title that has several (for example, contains Reality).
fieldHelp.imdb_rating: Always pair this with a vote floor. An 8.3 drawn from a few hundred votes is noise, not quality. Every library holds a few of them, and a rating floor on its own would keep every one of them, forever.
fieldHelp.imdb_votes: How many people rated it. A useful protection in its own right: a film with a million votes is culturally significant even if nobody here has watched it lately.
fieldHelp.on_list: Matches a list by the name it has on Settings → Lists.
fieldHelp.quality: The quality of the file on disk, as your library names it (for example Bluray-1080p, SDTV). Use "contains" to match a resolution: contains 2160p for 4K.
fieldHelp.recent_watchers: How many different people have watched this within your popularity window. Windowed on purpose: on a long-lived server almost everything has been watched by someone, eventually, so an all-time count protects nearly the whole library and the rule stops meaning anything. Only a fraction of those items still have watchers in the last year, and that is the number that tells you the title is still alive.
fieldHelp.release_age: How long ago the title was released. Pairs well with how long it has gone unwatched: old and untouched is a stronger case than either alone.
fieldHelp.requested: Whether someone asked for this through your requests app. If Reaper cannot tell, because the requests app is unreachable or this title could not be matched to a request, this is left unknown and never counts toward removal.
fieldHelp.season_rank: The newest season on disk is 1, the one before it 2, and so on. Keeping the last 2 seasons means 2 or less. Counted over seasons that actually hold files, specials excluded, never from what Sonarr planned to download.
fieldHelp.show_ended: Whether the series has finished for good. An ended show will get no new seasons to draw viewers back; a returning one still might. TV only.
fieldHelp.size_bytes: How much space this file occupies.
fieldHelp.streaming_now: Re-checked in the seconds before any delete, never only at scan time.
fieldHelp.watchers_all_time: Everyone who has ever watched this. It can only be used to keep a title, never to remove one. Using it to remove things would make recent viewing count for nothing.
fieldHelp.whitelisted: A tag list, a Plex collection, or your watchlist. Use "On one of your lists" to match one list by name; this is the yes/no over all of them.
